result: A multibyte sequence cut short (by an ASCII byte or end of file) keeps its bytes for byte reads on a wide stream, locale encoding and ccs=; col byte-identical to stock on all y23 inputs
informational: y23.sh itself (deb swap into a trixie root) not run: it needs this branch's .deb packages; replaced by the distribution's col (/usr/bin/col on the Skylake-SP host) under the branch's built libc through its loader, 6/6 cmp-identical to stock; the next snapshot's y23 run covers the swapped root
D-12.28 (reserved) amends D-12.27: at end of input inside a character the bytes go back too, matching the reference; the differences row lost its end-of-input clause
A ccs= stream also dropped every byte of an invalid sequence; fixed by the same give-back

impact.what: getc after getwc EILSEQ on a cut-short sequence (\xe2\x82 then t; \xc3 then '(') returns the sequence's first byte, not the ASCII byte; util-linux col output on y23's invalid input 44 bytes identical to stock (was 38)
getc after WEOF at end of input inside a character returns the character's bytes (was EOF); ccs= streams keep an invalid sequence's bytes (were dropped)
getc/fgetc per call (wl_percall stdio_char.c, Skylake-SP); putc family 26.1, unlocked forms 13.0-14.1 also unchanged
conformance checks added to s12_wide_byte_reads.c (col pass-through over six invalid kinds in two codecs, positions, ungetc, end of input) and plants

improvement: The y23 harness needs a deb build to test one libc change; a loader-run of the distribution binary against the role's target/niji gives the same answer in seconds and could be a standard step for Yohane follow-ups
next_step: land; the next snapshot's y23 run should show the invalid input identical to stock
